summary: This resolution expresses US support for Iranian protesters by commending their bravery, condemning the regime's killings and arrests, demanding prisoner releases and internet access, recognizing their right to choose their government through elections, and urging the US to coordinate with allies on measures to stop further lethal violence.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is a symbolic expression of support for Iranian protesters and condemnation of the regime. It contains no provisions, authorizations, or implications related to US government spending levels or budgets.
No references to taxes, tax policy, revenue measures, or fiscal changes appear in the bill text.
The bill addresses Iranian human rights and protests but makes no connection to US healthcare systems, coverage models, or policy.
No engagement with US gun regulations, rights, or firearms policy; the text concerns Iranian regime violence against protesters.
The resolution focuses exclusively on events inside Iran and contains zero provisions or implications for US immigration law or border policy.
No mention of reproductive rights, abortion access, or related US policy.
While the bill calls for 'concrete measures' to deter violence in Iran, it does not authorize, fund, or direct any change in US military or defense spending.
No environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions are present.
The bill does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or domestic social safety-net policy.
No references to schools, education funding, or US education policy.
No engagement with drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related US policy.
The resolution condemns Iranian repression and calls for release of political prisoners in Iran, but it does not alter or address US criminal justice statutes, sentencing, or policing.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are included.
The bill contains no fiscal measures that would affect deficits or the national debt.
The preamble notes repression of LGBTQ rights by the Iranian regime, but the resolution does not change or address US legal protections for LGBTQ individuals.
The bill urges diplomatic coordination and 'concrete measures' regarding Iran but does not authorize, expand, or reduce US foreign aid programs.
The text endorses free elections for the Iranian people but has no bearing on US voting access, election integrity rules, or electoral procedures.
The resolution supports internet access inside Iran but does not regulate US technology companies, data privacy, or domestic tech policy.
No provisions related to unions, worker protections, or labor policy in the United States.
The bill references freedom of religion in Iran but does not modify US religious liberty or anti-discrimination statutes.
